channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: itch.io Weekly New Games Roundup: Nov 2–8 (Part 2)
item.description: indienova rounds up the second half of the new games released on itch.io from Nov 2 to 8, including several indie titles built with Godot — worth a browse for developers looking for inspiration or gameplay references.

item.title: How to Reduce Mobile Game App Size: A Practical Guide
item.description: Measure before you cut: textures are usually the biggest share of a mobile game's size, followed by audio and meshes, with practical steps to trim each.

item.title: BOXERBOTS — Looking for Volunteer Game Developers!
item.description: A developer building BOXERBOTS, a first-person multiplayer robot fighting game in Unreal Engine 5.8, is recruiting volunteer developers — worth a look for anyone wanting hands-on multiplayer project experience.

item.title: Building Meu Acervo 3D: an open-source hub for 3D creators
item.description: An open-source hub that gathers 3D assets across Sketchfab, Poly Haven, and ambientCG, plus tools for creators.

item.title: How I built a "chess-engine" style AI for a 6-dice strategy game natively on my Pixel 9 Pro
item.description: A solo developer built an AI opponent for a six-dice tabletop game entirely on his phone, using chess-engine-style probability simulation instead of fixed rules — and teaching the AI to read the opponent’s scorecard and adjust its risk appetite on the fly.

item.title: Add Instant 'Game Feel' With This 6-Line JS Screen Shake & Hit-Stop Trick
item.description: No physics engine needed: just six lines of canvas translation shake inside your render loop to make weapon hits and collisions in a 2D HTML5 browser game feel ten times heavier.

item.title: Building NICHLYST: The Gate That Stayed Open — 33 Endings, 32 Green Tests, One Honest Caveat
item.description: After fixing 704 failing assertions, the author validates 33 endings and bilingual fields with a run of small, narrow checks — then admits the phase gates passed while a known device-side startup error still awaits a real device run, so green tests prove only what they prove.

item.title: Clannect Engine v0.2 Is Here: A Major Step Towards Open Release
item.description: Clannect Engine has reached v0.2, another key step toward its open release, and developers tracking small engines should keep an eye on its progress.

item.title: A Blackjack Table That Lives in a README, Dealt by GitHub Actions
item.description: A playable blackjack table that lives in a README: place a bet via an issue, a workflow reads it, and the README redraws the hand.

item.title: Roblox dropped a Studio Beta that generates R15 animations from text prompts AND converts old R6 animations to R15
item.description: Roblox added a Prompt-to-Animation beta to Studio Assistant: type a movement and mood description to generate R15 humanoid clips up to 10 seconds long, plus a neural-network tool that upscales old R6 animations to R15 — handy for solo devs who'd rather not keyframe from scratch.

item.title: How to Build a Gamified Fitness Mascot With Rive: A Developer's Guide
item.description: This tutorial shows how to use Rive state machines to build an interactive fitness mascot that evolves with progress, reacts to workouts and celebrates streaks, with developer-ready controls for React Native and Flutter.

item.title: How we made battles deterministic and server-verified in a Telegram mini-game
item.description: The Seraph Legion team explains how they made battles in their Telegram mini-game deterministic and server-verified: the client only sends intent while the server decides outcomes and replays the sim, a lesson learned after a farming exploit showed them never to trust client-side math.

item.title: Engineered in Japan GCC: Optimizing Unity WebGL / Emscripten JS Bridge (Zero-Copy FS & Branchless Lookup)
item.description: This technical report breaks down the JavaScript bridge bottleneck between the browser and the engine in Unity WebGL games, cutting memory use and CPU load with a zero-copy filesystem and branchless lookup — a useful reference for developers shipping games on the web.

item.title: How to Publish the Game You Just Built on Free Tiers — Lessons From 7,000 Players and One Dead Database
item.description: A postmortem on publishing a finished game on free tiers — leaderboards, servers, bills, and what a dead database taught the author.

item.title: How I made a text horror game in Twine (and what I'd do differently)
item.description: A data analyst shares how he built the text horror game FINAL CUT in Twine with SugarCube — branching narrative, state and sound — and what he would do differently next time.

item.title: What we learned measuring a location game: the metrics that actually tell you if it works
item.description: Location games can't be measured with sit-down app metrics — this piece shares which numbers actually show whether one works.

item.title: Best Godot AI coding assistants and MCP plugins (2026)
item.description: A roundup of Godot AI coding assistants and MCP plugins for indie devs, recommending free MCP plugins wired into an AI agent you already use.

item.title: Game Analytics: The Events Every Mobile Game Should Track
item.description: Mobile game analytics should start with a small planned set of events across six groups — sessions, first-launch funnel, progression, economy, monetization, and technical health.

item.title: Wild Shift Devlog #4: Don't lose your run
item.description: The fourth devlog for GitHub Game Off 2026 entry The Debugger 0x03: Wild Shift covers what not to lose during a run.

item.title: Generating a contact sheet for an osu! skin with Python and Pillow
item.description: An osu! skin can hold hundreds of PNGs, and checking them one by one is slow and easy to miss transparent-image gaps; the author shares a lightweight Python script that tiles every sprite onto one labeled checkerboard contact sheet and flags missing @2x assets along the way.
